Revisions of the trend as new data arrive

Source: R/trend_index.R
trend_revisions.Rd

Re-runs extract_trend() on the data truncated at each origin and compares the trend estimated with data up to the origin with the full-sample trend, at lags 0..max_lag weeks before the origin.

Usage

trend_revisions(
  dt,
  key_cols,
  time_col,
  value_col,
  origins,
  max_lag = 26L,
  scale = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

dt, key_cols, time_col, value_col

As in extract_trend().

origins

Vector of origins (Date, IDate or 'YYYY-MM-DD'), each equal to a time present in dt.

max_lag

Largest lag in weeks (non-negative integer).

scale

NULL, or a positive number (e.g. 100) to add revisions in index points.

...

Further arguments passed to extract_trend() (e.g. transform, method, harmonics).

Value

A data.table with columns key_cols, origin, lag, time_col, trend_full, trend_vintage, revision and, when scale is given, revision_index. Attribute summary: one row per lag with n, mean_revision, mean_abs_revision, rmse_revision and, when scale is given, mean_abs_revision_index.

Details

For origin o and lag h, the revision is trend_full(o - 7h) - trend_vintage(o - 7h) on the transformed scale. The size of the revision as a function of h tells how many final weeks of the trend are provisional. With harmonics = NULL the number of harmonics is re-selected at each origin, so revisions also include changes of K. When scale is given, revision_index expresses the revision in index points: scale * (exp(rev) - 1) for log, scale * (p_full / p_vintage - 1) for logit (shares) and scale * (full / vintage - 1) for none.

Examples

set.seed(1)
weeks <- data.table::as.IDate("2023-05-01") + 7L * (0:119)
d <- data.table::data.table(
  source = "a",
  week = weeks,
  n = exp(5 + 0.003 * seq_along(weeks) + rnorm(120, 0, 0.03))
)
rv <- trend_revisions(d, "source", "week", "n",
  origins = weeks[c(100, 110)], max_lag = 4L, harmonics = 0L
)
attr(rv, "summary")
#>      lag     n mean_revision mean_abs_revision rmse_revision
#>    <int> <int>         <num>             <num>         <num>
#> 1:     0     2  -0.002430196       0.003749066   0.004467813
#> 2:     1     2  -0.002299686       0.003466441   0.004159900
#> 3:     2     2  -0.002091307       0.003288027   0.003896753
#> 4:     3     2  -0.001846492       0.003166195   0.003665286
#> 5:     4     2  -0.001515442       0.003150494   0.003496023
